metrics.title: Coverage
metrics.description:
Share of the repository's commits that carry an AI-Attribution trailer at all — instrumented or not.

**This measures instrumentation, not AI use.** A commit with `status=undetermined` counts here: it has a trailer, it just records that no agent activity was found. Adoption beside it counts only `status=assisted`.

Measured per repository: whodunit 98.9%, nj-agents 99.0%, EngageHub 79.0% — EngageHub was instrumented later, so a fifth of its history predates the hooks. Commits made before `dun init` can never be covered.

The denominator is every commit the warehouse knows about for the repository, not every commit whodunit recorded. Dividing by the latter is what made this identical to adoption.

AND repo_id = rc.repo_id) LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha LEFT JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = w.repo_id WHERE (? = '__all__' OR r.contributor = ? OR w.commit_sha IS NULL) AND c.authored_date BETWEEN FROM_UNIXTIME(?) AND FROM_UNIXTIME(?)

metrics.sql: WITH c AS ( SELECT c.status, c.repo_id, c.commit_sha, COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) AS person, COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') AS team, c.committed_at, DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) AS d, DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY) AS w FROM whodunit_commits c LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id LEFT JOIN whodunit_teams wt ON wt.contributor = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND c.contributor IS NOT NULL AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') AND (? = '__all__' OR c.method = ?) AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) = ?) AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') = ?)) SELECT CAST(w AS DATETIME) AS time, ROUND(100*SUM(status='assisted')/COUNT(*),0) AS `Assisted share`, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status='assisted' THEN person END) AS `People using it` FROM c GROUP BY w HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY time

metrics.description: One row per person, one cell per week: green when they made an assisted commit that week, grey when they committed without one, blank when they did not commit. Retention is readable as horizontal runs of green; a row that goes green then grey is someone who tried it and stopped. Filter by team when the roster is large.

metrics.title: Coverage
metrics.description:
Share of the repository's commits that carry an AI-Attribution trailer at all — instrumented or not.

**This measures instrumentation, not AI use.** A commit with `status=undetermined` counts here: it has a trailer, it just records that no agent activity was found. Adoption beside it counts only `status=assisted`.

Measured per repository: whodunit 98.9%, nj-agents 99.0%, EngageHub 79.0% — EngageHub was instrumented later, so a fifth of its history predates the hooks. Commits made before `dun init` can never be covered.

The denominator is every commit the warehouse knows about for the repository, not every commit whodunit recorded. Dividing by the latter is what made this identical to adoption.

metrics.title: Issues compared · AI-assisted
metrics.description:
**How many issues are in this cohort** — the denominator for the median beside it.

Shown deliberately rather than tucked into a tooltip. A median over a handful of issues moves hours on one or two of them, and a cohort of zero means there is no comparison at all — the Delta would be measuring nothing. Check this number before reading anything into the medians.

This panel counts issues **carrying an AI-attribution trailer**.

**How an issue is classified.** Its key is matched against commit messages (`WHO-12` in a commit subject links that commit to that issue). If any linked commit carries `status=assisted`, the issue counts as AI-assisted; otherwise it counts as not. An issue whose key appears in no commit message is in neither cohort — it is absent, not counted as unassisted.

**Scope.** Issues closed within the dashboard time range, on the selected issue board. The Repository filter does not apply: an issue's commits can span repositories, so filtering by one would drop genuinely assisted issues and understate the comparison.

AND bi.board_id = ? AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL AND i.resolution_date BETWEEN ? AND ? AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' AND i.issue_key REGEXP CONCAT('^', (SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(i2.issue_key,'-',1) FROM issues i2 JOIN board_issues bi2 ON bi2.issue_id = i2.id WHERE bi2.board_id = ? AND i2.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' LIMIT 1), '-[0-9]+$') GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes HAVING ai = 1 ) t

metrics.sql: SELECT ROUND( (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.contributor) FROM whodunit_events e WHERE e.observed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 86400) * 1000000000 AND (? = '__all__' OR e.contributor = ?)) * 100.0 / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.contributor) FROM whodunit_events e WHERE e.observed_at >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 30*86400) * 1000000000 AND (? = '__all__' OR e.contributor = ?)), 0), 1) v

metrics.title: MCP calls
metrics.description: Calls to connected MCP servers. A total, not a breakdown: the transcripts name each server, but the collector keeps only file-editing tools today.

metrics.sql: SELECT SUM(s.mcp_calls) v FROM whodunit_sessions s LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor WHERE s.last_seen BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = ?)

metrics.title: Distinct tools
metrics.description: File-editing tools seen. Skills, chat and search are called as tools too and are visible in the transcripts, but are not collected yet.

metrics.title: Session engagement
metrics.description: How a session was actually worked, from counts only — no message text is ever recorded. 'Turns per prompt' is agent messages per human message: a high number means long autonomous runs, a low one means tight back-and-forth (NAV-55).

params_schema.name: contributor
params_schema.description: Filter by contributor; '__all__' (the default) matches everything.

metrics.sql: SELECT LEFT(s.session,8) AS `Session`, FROM_UNIXTIME(s.first_seen/1000000000) AS `Started`, ROUND((s.last_seen-s.first_seen)/60000000000) AS `Minutes`, s.user_messages AS `Prompts`, s.agent_messages AS `Agent msgs`, ROUND(s.agent_messages/NULLIF(s.user_messages,0),1) AS `Turns per prompt`, s.tool_calls AS `Tool calls`, s.distinct_tools AS `Distinct tools`, s.mcp_calls AS `MCP calls` FROM whodunit_sessions s LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor WHERE (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = ?) AND s.first_seen BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 ORDER BY s.first_seen DESC

metrics.title: Coverage
metrics.description: Share of commits in instrumented repositories that carry an AI-Attribution trailer of any kind, including the states meaning no evidence was available. **Coverage is not adoption** — a repository at 100% may have had no agent involvement at all. It says the instrumentation is working, nothing more.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT w.commit_sha) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT c.sha), 0), 1) AS coverage FROM commits c JOIN repo_commits rc ON rc.commit_sha = c.sha JOIN repo_commits rc2 ON rc2.repo_id = rc.repo_id JOIN whodunit_commits seen ON seen.commit_sha = rc2.commit_sha LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha WHERE c.authored_date BETWEEN FROM_UNIXTIME(?) AND FROM_UNIXTIME(?)

metrics.title: Penetration
metrics.description: Share of commits with a real verdict that are AI-assisted. The denominator is `assisted` + `unassisted` + `unmatched` — all three mean the tool looked and reached an answer. `uninstrumented` and `undetermined` are excluded: it never looked, so counting them would understate this. Read it beside Coverage.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(status = 'assisted') / NULLIF(SUM(status IN ('assisted','unassisted','unmatched')), 0) AS penetration FROM whodunit_commits WHERE committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000

metrics.title: Commits
metrics.description: Total commits in the selected window, whether or not they carry a trailer.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS commits FROM whodunit_commits WHERE committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000

metrics.title: Median agent share
metrics.description: Median ratio across commits that have one. Ratio is the share of a commit's changed lines matching text an agent produced — overlap, not authorship. A line the agent wrote and a developer then edited counts as the developer's. Commits with no line-level evidence are excluded, not counted as zero.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT AVG(t.ratio) AS median_share FROM ( SELECT c.ratio, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY c.ratio) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.ratio IS NOT NULL AND c.committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 ) t WHERE t.rn IN (FLOOR((t.n + 1) / 2), CEIL((t.n + 1) / 2))

metrics.title: Evidence mix
metrics.description: How much evidence stands behind each commit, strongest first: intersected, observed, declared, inferred — then the states meaning there is none. Read it beside any penetration figure: a number resting on `declared` is a different claim from one resting on `intersected`.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END AS state, COUNT(*) AS commits FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END ORDER BY commits DESC

metrics.title: Agent share of lines, per assisted commit
metrics.description: Every assisted commit with a known share, binned by how much of it the agent wrote. A cluster near one is whole commits handed over; a cluster in the middle is collaboration; two humps is two ways of working on one team. The median above is one point on this shape.

params_schema.name: time_from

metrics.title: Assisted commits with a known share, and without
metrics.description: How many assisted commits carry a share of lines and how many do not. A share needs line-level evidence; a commit attributed by weaker means has none, and is counted here rather than given a zero.

metrics.title: Agent share by work type
metrics.description: Average agent share of lines per assisted commit, by purpose. Which kinds of work get handed over whole and which stay collaborative. Purposes with under 5 commits are omitted.

GROUP BY c.purpose HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY value DESC

metrics.title: Evidence strength by agent
metrics.description: Assisted commits per agent, split by how they were attributed. Agents differ in what they record, so the strongest tier is not equally available to all — an agent that never reaches intersected is one whose transcript does not carry line hashes.

metrics.sql: SELECT c.agent AS metric, SUM(c.method='intersected') AS `intersected`, SUM(c.method='observed') AS `observed`, SUM(c.method='inferred') AS `inferred`, SUM(c.method='declared') AS `declared` FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND c.status='assisted' AND c.agent <> '' AND (? = '__all__' OR c.method = ?) GROUP BY c.agent ORDER BY SUM(1) DESC

metrics.title: Evidence by repository
metrics.description: Per repository: assisted share, how much of that assisted work reached the strongest tier, and the share of commits the tool gave no verdict on. A high no-verdict share is a repository where the tool is not installed or not reaching the transcripts.

metrics.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT c.* FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') AND (? = '__all__' OR c.method = ?)), nm AS (SELECT c.repo_id, MAX(rp.name) name FROM c JOIN repo_commits rc ON rc.commit_sha = c.commit_sha JOIN repos rp ON rp.id = rc.repo_id GROUP BY c.repo_id) SELECT COALESCE(nm.name, LEFT(c.repo_id,8)) AS `Repository`, COUNT(*) AS `Commits`, ROUND(100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*),0) AS `Assisted %`, ROUND(100*SUM(c.method='intersected')/NULLIF(SUM(c.status='assisted'),0),0) AS `Intersected, of assisted %`, ROUND(100*SUM(c.status IN ('undetermined','uninstrumented','degraded'))/COUNT(*),0) AS `No verdict %` FROM c LEFT JOIN nm ON nm.repo_id = c.repo_id GROUP BY c.repo_id, nm.name ORDER BY `Commits` DESC

metrics.title: Evidence mix over time
metrics.description: Commits per day by evidence state. A drop in the stronger states without a drop in commit volume usually means an adapter stopped recognising its agent's format, not that people stopped using agents.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(c.committed_at / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400) AS time, CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY time, CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END ORDER BY time

metrics.title: Most agent-edited files
metrics.description: Per-file agent activity, from observed edits rather than commits. A file with many edits and few committed lines is one the agent iterated on heavily — that is effort, not output.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(file, '/', -1) AS file, COUNT(*) AS agent_edits, SUM(lines_added) AS lines_written FROM whodunit_events WHERE file <> '' AND observed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY file ORDER BY agent_edits DESC LIMIT 20

metrics.title: Adoption, week by week
metrics.description: Share of all commits with verified AI assistance, per week. The S-curve the rest of the page is read against.

metrics.title: This week
metrics.description: Assisted share of commits in the last 7 days — the latest point on the adoption curve, on its own so it can be quoted.
metrics.sql: SELECT ROUND(100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at > (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 7*86400)*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded')

metrics.title: People using it
metrics.description: Contributors with at least one verified AI-assisted commit in range, against everyone who committed. Counts people, not licences.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.status='assisted' THEN c.contributor END) AS `Using AI`, COUNT(DISTINCT c.contributor) AS `Active` FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND c.contributor IS NOT NULL AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded')

metrics.title: Deployment frequency — per week
metrics.description: Deployments per week over the selected range. Band per DORA 2023: Elite is on demand (daily or more), High is daily to weekly, Medium weekly to monthly, Low under monthly.

params_schema.name: time_from_dt
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window, as a DATETIME literal — required alongside time_from_dt whenever a query also binds time_from/time_to for the same window; see time_from.

params_schema.name: time_to_dt
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window, as a DATETIME literal.

metrics.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN per_day >= 1 THEN 'Elite — on demand' WHEN per_day >= 1/7 THEN 'High — daily to weekly' WHEN per_day >= 1/30 THEN 'Medium — weekly to monthly' ELSE 'Low — under monthly' END AS metric, ROUND(per_day*7,1) AS value FROM (SELECT COUNT(*)/GREATEST(DATEDIFF(MAX(finished_date),MIN(finished_date)),1) per_day FROM cicd_deployment_commits WHERE finished_date BETWEEN ? AND ?) t

metrics.title: Lead time for changes — hours
metrics.description: Mean pull-request cycle time, first commit to deployed, from DevLake's PR metrics. Band per DORA 2023: Elite under a day, High under a week, Medium under a month.

params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window, as a DATETIME literal — required alongside time_from_dt whenever a query also binds time_from/time_to for the same window; see time_from.

params_schema.name: time_to_dt
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window, as a DATETIME literal.

metrics.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN hrs < 24 THEN 'Elite — under a day' WHEN hrs < 168 THEN 'High — under a week' WHEN hrs < 720 THEN 'Medium — under a month' ELSE 'Low — over a month' END AS metric, ROUND(hrs,1) AS value FROM (SELECT AVG(pr_cycle_time)/60 hrs FROM project_pr_metrics WHERE pr_cycle_time IS NOT NULL AND pr_merged_date BETWEEN ? AND ?) t

AND ?) t

metrics.title: Time to restore — hours
metrics.description: Mean time from incident opened to resolved. Band per DORA 2023: Elite under an hour, High under a day, Medium under a week. Rests on few incidents; moves a lot with each one.

AND ?) t

AND ? GROUP BY w) SELECT CAST(m.w AS DATETIME) AS time, ROUND(m.v,1) AS `Deployments`, ROUND(a.share,0) AS `Assisted share` FROM m LEFT JOIN a ON a.w = m.w ORDER BY time

metrics.title: Throughput per week, before and after
metrics.description: Average per week on each side of the adoption date, for the three things that have history on both sides. Adoption date is derived from the data. A difference, not an effect: team size and work mix also changed.

metrics.sql: WITH adopt AS ( SELECT MIN(w) AS d FROM ( SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w, SUM(status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY w HAVING share >= 0.25) t), iss AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN i.resolution_date >= adopt.d THEN 'after' ELSE 'before' END side, COUNT(*)/GREATEST(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.resolution_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.resolution_date) DAY)),1) per_week FROM issues i CROSS JOIN adopt WHERE i.status='DONE' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND i.resolution_date BETWEEN ? AND ? GROUP BY side), com AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9) >= adopt.d THEN 'after' ELSE 'before' END side, COUNT(*)/GREATEST(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY)),1) per_week FROM whodunit_commits c CROSS JOIN adopt WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') GROUP BY side), pr AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN p.pr_merged_date >= adopt.d THEN 'after' ELSE 'before' END side, COUNT(*)/GREATEST(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_SUB(DATE(p.pr_merged_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(p.pr_merged_date) DAY)),1) per_week FROM project_pr_metrics p CROSS JOIN adopt WHERE p.pr_merged_date IS NOT NULL AND p.pr_merged_date BETWEEN ? AND ? metrics.title: Total tokens
metrics.description:
Every token billed: uncached input + cache reads + cache writes + output.

**Almost all of it is cache reads.** Measured here: 7.53B cache reads, 54.6M cache writes, 13.2M uncached input, 7.9M output — so this number tracks how much context was re-sent, not how much the models produced. The four tiles to the right hold the same breakdown as live figures.

Tokens, not currency: under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so a price table would report money nobody spent. Multiply by your own contract if you need a figure.

metrics.title: Output tokens
metrics.description:
What the models actually produced, as opposed to what was re-sent to them.

Typically a fraction of a percent of the total — 0.1% measured here.

**Total and Output are three orders of magnitude apart**, so they render in different units (B against M) and comparing them by eye reads as a contradiction. They are not: 7.6 B is a thousand times 7.6 M.

metrics.title: Cache write payback
metrics.description:
Reads returned per token written to cache — a **ratio, not a percentage**. 135 means each cached token was read back 135 times.

Below 1.25x the writes cost more than they saved — a write is billed at about 1.25x base and a read at 0.1x.

**The obvious break-even of 1.0 is wrong**: a series at 1.10x lost money while looking healthy.

Empty for Codex, which reports cache reads but never writes.

AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') = ?) GROUP BY time, s.model ORDER BY time, s.model

This is the efficiency figure per model: a model that costs more per token can still cost less per line if it needs fewer tokens to get there. Lines are attributed by the model on the event.

metrics.sql: WITH sp AS (SELECT s.model, SUM((COALESCE(s.input_tokens,0)/1e6*p.input_usd + COALESCE(s.output_tokens,0)/1e6*p.output_usd + COALESCE(s.cache_read_tokens,0)/1e6*p.cache_read_usd + COALESCE(s.cache_write_tokens,0)/1e6*p.cache_write_usd)) usd, SUM(s.output_tokens) out_tok FROM whodunit_sessions s LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id LEFT JOIN whodunit_teams wt ON wt.contributor = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) LEFT JOIN whodunit_model_prices p ON p.model = s.model WHERE s.last_seen BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND s.input_tokens IS NOT NULL AND p.model IS NOT NULL AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = ?) AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') = ?) GROUP BY s.model), ln AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(e.model,''),'(no model)') model, SUM(e.lines_added) added FROM whodunit_events e LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = e.contributor LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, e.contributor) LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id LEFT JOIN whodunit_teams wt ON wt.contributor = COALESCE(wi.canonical, e.contributor) WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND e.lines_added > 0 AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, e.contributor) = ?) AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') = ?) GROUP BY model) SELECT sp.model AS `Model`, ROUND(sp.usd,2) AS `List-price spend`, ln.added AS `Lines the agent wrote`, ROUND(sp.usd/NULLIF(ln.added/1000,0),2) AS `$ per 1,000 agent lines`, ROUND(sp.out_tok/NULLIF(ln.added,0),0) AS `Output tokens per line` FROM sp LEFT JOIN ln ON ln.model = sp.model ORDER BY sp.usd DESC

metrics.title: Total tokens
metrics.description:
Every token billed: uncached input + cache reads + cache writes + output.

**Almost all of it is cache reads.** Measured here: 7.53B cache reads, 54.6M cache writes, 13.2M uncached input, 7.9M output — so this number tracks how much context was re-sent, not how much the models produced. The four tiles to the right hold the same breakdown as live figures.

Tokens, not currency: under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so a price table would report money nobody spent. Multiply by your own contract if you need a figure.

metrics.description:

**The obvious break-even of 1.0 is wrong**: a series at 1.10x lost money while looking healthy.

metrics.title: Sessions that compacted
metrics.description:
Share of sessions whose context was compacted at least once (NAV-106).

**Read this beside the context the sessions were running at.** A long session costs more even when cached, because the whole context is re-sent every turn — and compacting is the one thing a person can do about it. Measured on this machine, 92% of turns ran above 150k context while a small fraction of sessions ever compacted.

**Deliberately not colour-coded.** A low rate is only a problem alongside high context, and this panel cannot see context — a short session has nothing to compact, and colouring 8% red would call that a failure. The number is the finding; the judgement needs the context distribution, which the journal cannot answer per turn yet.

The denominator counts only sessions from agents that report the signal at all. Antigravity has no equivalent and is excluded rather than counted as never compacting.

Ordered by total tokens, so the largest consumer is at the top even though every bar is the same length.

metrics.description:
Where the agent's output actually landed, top twelve branches by lines written, with everything below them summed into a final bar.

That last bar is there so the top twelve reads as a slice rather than as everything — the failure the old table's silent LIMIT 25 already caused once. Measured here the twelve are 90% of all lines written across 42 branches.

Branches contributing zero lines are excluded — those are sessions that read and ran things without writing, which the events count already covers elsewhere.

Long branch names are truncated for the axis; the tooltip carries the value and the panel beside this one says how much sits outside the top twelve.

metrics.title: Autonomy granted — tool calls per session
metrics.description:
How much work happens per session at each level of autonomy.

**One metric rather than two bars.** Sessions and total tool calls run in opposite directions here — 64 sessions on Codex's `never` produced 506 calls, 2 Claude Code sessions on `auto` produced 6,766 — so charting both put a 13x range beside a 32x one and flattened whichever shared the axis. Dividing them gives the thing both were circling: 8 calls per session on `never`, 3,383 on `auto`.

The ladder is monotonic across every mode measured, which is the finding: autonomy is not how often it is granted, it is how much happens once it is.

The agent is in the label because each mode belongs to exactly one — Codex says `never` and `on-request`, Claude Code says `acceptEdits`, `auto` and `default`. Each agent's own vocabulary is kept rather than mapped onto a shared enum: asserting that `never` means the same as `default` would invent a comparison neither agent made.

metrics.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000), ?) AS `period`, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.status='assisted' AND e.agent='claude-code' THEN c.commit_sha END)*100.0 /NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.committed_at >= b.first_attributed AND e.agent='claude-code' THEN c.commit_sha END),0),1) AS `claude-code`, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.status='assisted' AND e.agent='codex' THEN c.commit_sha END)*100.0 /NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.committed_at >= b.first_attributed AND e.agent='codex' THEN c.commit_sha END),0),1) AS `codex` FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN (SELECT repo_id, MIN(CASE WHEN method <> 'undetermined' THEN committed_at END) AS first_attributed FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY repo_id) b ON b.repo_id=c.repo_id JOIN whodunit_events e ON e.repo_id=c.repo_id AND e.observed_at BETWEEN c.committed_at - 86400000000000 AND c.committed_at WHERE (? = '__all__' OR c.method = ?) metrics.title: Output tokens per delivered line
metrics.description:
Output tokens spent per line of assisted work that **reached a commit**.

The denominator is what distinguishes this from the token-per-attributed-line panel above: that one divides by agent activity, this one by work that shipped. Tokens spent on edits that were abandoned or rewritten count in the numerator and not the denominator, which is the point — that gap is the cost of work that did not land.

Tokens, never currency: under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so a price table would report money nobody spent.

Sessions and commits are counted over the same window but are not joined row-to-row — a session can span commits and a commit can span sessions. Read it as a rate for the period, not as an attribution per commit.

metrics.title: Output tokens per 1,000 attributed lines
metrics.description:
What the agent spent, in tokens, per thousand lines it wrote.

**This replaced a dollar figure** derived from a hand-typed monthly spend divided evenly over every line — an allocation dressed as a measurement, which reported the same unit cost whether the agent ran once or a thousand times, and defaulted to a $200 placeholder that was nobody's actual bill.

Tokens rather than currency, deliberately: under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so multiplying by an API rate would report money nobody spent — and nothing in a transcript says which billing model a user is on. Multiply by your own contract if you need a figure.

Empty where no session reported tokens: Antigravity reports none at all, and that is a property of the agent rather than a gap.

**Read the crossover, not the totals.** Unbanded, assisted work looks better — 28.4% against 33.3% — but that is a size-mix artefact: assisted commits skew larger, and large commits are rarely labelled fixes. Banded, assisted is lower at small and large sizes and higher in the middle.

metrics.title: Issues opened vs closed · $board
metrics.description:
Issues opened and closed per period, on the selected board.

**Closed means closed in that period, whatever period it was opened in.** Measured here, 141 of 240 issues over three months — so the bars are not a matched pair and the gap between them is not this period's arithmetic.

metrics.sql: WITH o AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.created_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.created_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) n FROM issues i WHERE i.created_date IS NOT NULL AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' GROUP BY w), c AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.resolution_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.resolution_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) n FROM issues i WHERE i.status='DONE' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' GROUP BY w), wk AS (SELECT w FROM o UNION SELECT w FROM c), cum AS (SELECT wk.w, SUM(COALESCE(o.n,0)) OVER (ORDER BY wk.w) opened_cum, SUM(COALESCE(c.n,0)) OVER (ORDER BY wk.w) closed_cum, COALESCE(o.n,0) opened, COALESCE(c.n,0) closed FROM wk LEFT JOIN o ON o.w = wk.w LEFT JOIN c ON c.w = wk.w) SELECT CAST(w AS DATETIME) AS time, opened_cum - closed_cum AS `Open backlog`, closed - opened AS `Net flow` FROM cum WHERE w BETWEEN ? AND ? ORDER BY time

metrics.sql: WITH RECURSIVE o AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.created_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.created_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) n FROM issues i WHERE i.created_date IS NOT NULL AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' GROUP BY w), c AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.resolution_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.resolution_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) n FROM issues i WHERE i.status='DONE' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' GROUP BY w), wk AS (SELECT w FROM o UNION SELECT w FROM c), cum AS (SELECT wk.w, SUM(COALESCE(o.n,0)) OVER (ORDER BY wk.w) oc, SUM(COALESCE(c.n,0)) OVER (ORDER BY wk.w) cc FROM wk LEFT JOIN o ON o.w = wk.w LEFT JOIN c ON c.w = wk.w), last AS (SELECT MAX(w) w FROM cum), seed AS (SELECT last.w, cum.cc, cum.oc, (SELECT AVG(c.n) FROM c WHERE c.w > DATE_SUB(last.w, INTERVAL 8 WEEK)) cr, (SELECT AVG(o.n) FROM o WHERE o.w > DATE_SUB(last.w, INTERVAL 8 WEEK)) orate FROM last JOIN cum ON cum.w = last.w), proj AS (SELECT 0 k, w, cc, oc, cr, orate FROM seed UNION ALL SELECT k+1, DATE_ADD(w, INTERVAL 1 WEEK), cc + cr, oc + orate, cr, orate FROM proj WHERE k < 26 AND cc < oc) SELECT CAST(w AS DATETIME) AS time, oc AS `Opened, cumulative`, cc AS `Closed, cumulative`, CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL) AS `Closed, projected`, CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL) AS `Opened, projected` FROM cum WHERE w BETWEEN ? AND ? UNION ALL SELECT CAST(w AS DATETIME), NULL, NULL, ROUND(cc), ROUND(oc) FROM proj WHERE k > 0 ORDER BY time

metrics.title: Drain date under three rates
metrics.description: Open issues now, divided by net flow — closing rate minus the recent opening rate — under three closing rates: what the team did before adoption, the last 8 weeks, and its best recent 4 weeks. 'Never at this rate' means issues arrive faster than that rate closes them. Assumes inflow continues as it has.
metrics.sql: WITH adopt AS ( SELECT MIN(w) AS d FROM ( SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w, SUM(status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY w HAVING share >= 0.25) t), o AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.created_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.created_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) n FROM issues i WHERE i.created_date IS NOT NULL AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' GROUP BY w), c AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.resolution_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.resolution_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) n FROM issues i WHERE i.status='DONE' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$' GROUP BY w), last AS (SELECT MAX(w) w FROM c), open_now AS (SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM issues i WHERE i.status <> 'DONE' AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'), inflow AS (SELECT AVG(n) n FROM o, last WHERE o.w > DATE_SUB(last.w, INTERVAL 8 WEEK)), rates AS ( SELECT 'Pre-adoption throughput' scenario, 1 ord, (SELECT AVG(c.n) FROM c, adopt WHERE c.w < adopt.d) r UNION ALL SELECT 'Current, last 8 weeks', 2, (SELECT AVG(c.n) FROM c, last WHERE c.w > DATE_SUB(last.w, INTERVAL 8 WEEK)) UNION ALL SELECT 'Best recent 4 weeks', 3, (SELECT MAX(s) FROM (SELECT AVG(n) OVER (ORDER BY w ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) s FROM c) t)) SELECT scenario AS `Rate`, ROUND(r,1) AS `Closed / week`, ROUND(inflow.n,1) AS `Opened / week`, ROUND(r - inflow.n,1) AS `Net / week`, open_now.n AS `Open now`, CASE WHEN r - inflow.n > 0 THEN CEIL(open_now.n/(r - inflow.n)) END AS `Weeks to drain`, CASE WHEN r - inflow.n > 0 THEN DATE_FORMAT(DATE_ADD(last.w, INTERVAL CEIL(open_now.n/(r - inflow.n)) WEEK),'%b %e, %Y') ELSE 'never at this rate' END AS `Drains by` FROM rates, inflow, open_now, last ORDER BY ord

metrics.title: Drain date by team
metrics.description: Open issues per team by tracker assignee, against that team's closing and opening rates over the last 8 weeks. The (unassigned) row is every open issue with no assignee — usually most of them — and is the honest size of what cannot be forecast per team until the tracker assigns work. 'Never at this rate' means the team's inflow outruns its closing.

**A pre-instrumentation baseline is not a no-AI baseline.** Commits in that window may have been AI-assisted and simply not recorded, so it is a comparison against 'before we measured', not against 'before we used it'.

metrics.title: Acceptance
metrics.description:
Share of decided tool calls that were accepted.

**The denominator is decided calls only** — accepted, rejected or failed — not all calls. A call whose outcome was never recorded is excluded rather than counted as accepted, which would flatter the rate. See Decided tool calls beside this for the size of that denominator.

A rejection is a human declining; a failure is the tool erroring. Both count as decided, and only acceptance is in the numerator.

metrics.title: Issues opened vs closed
metrics.description:
Issues opened and closed per period, on the selected board.

**Closed means closed in that period, whatever period it was opened in.** Measured here, 141 of 240 issues over three months — so the bars are not a matched pair and the gap between them is not this period's arithmetic.

Scoped by issue board rather than repository: an issue is reachable from a repository only through its commits, and most issues have none — 109 of 379 here. A repository filter would silently drop the rest.

metrics.sql: WITH c AS ( SELECT c.purpose, CASE WHEN c.files_changed < 3 THEN '1-2 files' WHEN c.files_changed <= 20 THEN '3-20 files' ELSE '20+ files' END band, c.status, c.lines_added + c.lines_removed AS churn, c.files_changed AS files, COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) AS person, COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') AS team, c.committed_at, DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1000000000)) AS d FROM whodunit_commits c LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = c.contributor LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id LEFT JOIN whodunit_teams wt ON wt.contributor = COALESCE(wi.canonical, c.contributor) WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ?*1000000000 AND ?*1000000000 AND c.contributor IS NOT NULL AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') AND CASE c.status WHEN 'assisted' THEN 1 WHEN 'unassisted' THEN 1 END = 1 AND (? = '__all__' OR c.contributor = ?) AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') = ?) ), agg AS ( SELECT status, COUNT(*) commits, SUM(churn) total_lines, SUM(files) files, COUNT(DISTINCT person, d) person_days FROM c GROUP BY status ), n AS (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN status='assisted' THEN commits END) na, MAX(CASE WHEN status='unassisted' THEN commits END) nu FROM agg) SELECT d.definition AS metric, CASE WHEN d.u > 0 AND n.na >= 5 AND n.nu >= 5 THEN ROUND(100*(d.a-d.u)/d.u,0) END AS value FROM ( SELECT 'Commits per person-day' definition, 1 ord, MAX(CASE WHEN status='assisted' THEN commits/NULLIF(person_days,0) END) a, MAX(CASE WHEN status='unassisted' THEN commits/NULLIF(person_days,0) END) u FROM agg UNION ALL SELECT 'Lines per person-day', 2, MAX(CASE WHEN status='assisted' THEN total_lines/NULLIF(person_days,0) END), MAX(CASE WHEN status='unassisted' THEN total_lines/NULLIF(person_days,0) END) FROM agg UNION ALL SELECT 'Lines per commit', 3, MAX(CASE WHEN status='assisted' THEN total_lines/NULLIF(commits,0) END), MAX(CASE WHEN status='unassisted' THEN total_lines/NULLIF(commits,0) END) FROM agg UNION ALL SELECT 'Files per commit', 4, MAX(CASE WHEN status='assisted' THEN files/NULLIF(commits,0) END), MAX(CASE WHEN status='unassisted' THEN files/NULLIF(commits,0) END) FROM agg UNION ALL SELECT 'Files per person-day', 5, MAX(CASE WHEN status='assisted' THEN files/NULLIF(person_days,0) END), MAX(CASE WHEN status='unassisted' THEN files/NULLIF(person_days,0) END) FROM agg ) d CROSS JOIN n ORDER BY d.ord

metrics.title: Pooled vs conditioned
metrics.description: The same difference computed two ways. Pooled compares all assisted work against all unassisted work. Conditioned compares only like with like — same work type, same complexity band — and reweights onto a common mix. The gap between them is how much of the pooled figure was the mix of work each cohort picked up, rather than how productive it was. Neither is a verdict; both are differences between self-selected cohorts. Output here is lines delivered, not commits: inside a single work-type and complexity cell most contributor-days hold one commit, so a commit count pins both sides near 1 and measures the grid rather than the work.

metrics.title: Pooled vs conditioned
metrics.description: The same difference computed two ways. Pooled compares all assisted work against all unassisted work. Conditioned compares only like with like — same work type, same complexity band — and reweights onto a common mix. The gap between them is how much of the pooled figure was the mix of work each cohort picked up, rather than how productive it was. Neither is a verdict; both are differences between self-selected cohorts. Output here is lines delivered, not commits: inside a single work-type and complexity cell most contributor-days hold one commit, so a commit count pins both sides near 1 and measures the grid rather than the work.

metrics.sql: SELECT COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`, SUM(s.permission_mode = 'plan') AS `plan`, SUM(s.permission_mode = 'default') AS `default`, SUM(s.permission_mode = 'acceptEdits') AS `acceptEdits`, SUM(s.permission_mode = 'bypassPermissions') AS `bypassPermissions` FROM whodunit_sessions s LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id LEFT JOIN whodunit_teams wt ON wt.contributor = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) WHERE s.permission_mode IS NOT NULL AND s.first_seen BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') = ?) AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = ?) GROUP BY COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') ORDER BY `team`

metrics.title: Reasoning effort, where the agent reports it
metrics.description: Effort per team, from the agents that report it — Codex alone does, so this panel covers a subset by design and is not a gap. Higher effort spends more tokens on the same task, which is the lever behind cost differences between teams running the same work.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: team
params_schema.description: Filter by team; '__all__' (the default) matches everything.

params_schema.name: contributor
params_schema.description: Filter by contributor; '__all__' (the default) matches everything.

metrics.sql: SELECT COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') AS `team`, SUM(s.effort = 'low') AS `low`, SUM(s.effort = 'medium') AS `medium`, SUM(s.effort = 'high') AS `high` FROM whodunit_sessions s LEFT JOIN whodunit_identities wi ON wi.alias = s.contributor LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id LEFT JOIN whodunit_teams wt ON wt.contributor = COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) WHERE s.effort IS NOT NULL AND s.first_seen BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') = ?) AND (? = '__all__' OR COALESCE(wi.canonical, s.contributor) = ?) GROUP BY COALESCE(wt.team_name, t.name, '(unassigned)') ORDER BY `team`

metrics.title: Coverage
metrics.description: Share of commits in instrumented repositories that carry an AI-Attribution trailer of any kind, including the states meaning no evidence was available. **Coverage is not adoption** — a repository at 100% may have had no agent involvement at all. It says the instrumentation is working, nothing more.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT w.commit_sha) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT c.sha), 0), 1) AS coverage FROM commits c JOIN repo_commits rc ON rc.commit_sha = c.sha JOIN repo_commits rc2 ON rc2.repo_id = rc.repo_id JOIN whodunit_commits seen ON seen.commit_sha = rc2.commit_sha LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = c.sha WHERE c.authored_date BETWEEN FROM_UNIXTIME(?) AND FROM_UNIXTIME(?)

metrics.title: Penetration
metrics.description: Share of commits with a real verdict that are AI-assisted. The denominator is `assisted` + `unassisted` + `unmatched` — all three mean the tool looked and reached an answer. `uninstrumented` and `undetermined` are excluded: it never looked, so counting them would understate this. Read it beside Coverage.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(status = 'assisted') / NULLIF(SUM(status IN ('assisted','unassisted','unmatched')), 0) AS penetration FROM whodunit_commits WHERE committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000

metrics.title: Commits
metrics.description: Total commits in the selected window, whether or not they carry a trailer.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS commits FROM whodunit_commits WHERE committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000

metrics.title: Median agent share
metrics.description: Median ratio across commits that have one. Ratio is the share of a commit's changed lines matching text an agent produced — overlap, not authorship. A line the agent wrote and a developer then edited counts as the developer's. Commits with no line-level evidence are excluded, not counted as zero.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT AVG(t.ratio) AS median_share FROM ( SELECT c.ratio, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY c.ratio) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.ratio IS NOT NULL AND c.committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 ) t WHERE t.rn IN (FLOOR((t.n + 1) / 2), CEIL((t.n + 1) / 2))

metrics.title: Evidence mix
metrics.description: How much evidence stands behind each commit, strongest first: intersected, observed, declared, inferred — then the states meaning there is none. Read it beside any penetration figure: a number resting on `declared` is a different claim from one resting on `intersected`.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END AS state, COUNT(*) AS commits FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END ORDER BY commits DESC

metrics.title: Purpose distribution
metrics.description: What kind of work the commits were. Coverage without this is close to meaningless: 80% AI-assisted reads very differently when it is tests and config than when it is core feature logic.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT purpose, COUNT(*) AS commits FROM whodunit_commits WHERE committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY purpose ORDER BY commits DESC

metrics.title: Evidence mix over time
metrics.description: Commits per day by evidence state. A drop in the stronger states without a drop in commit volume usually means an adapter stopped recognising its agent's format, not that people stopped using agents.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(FLOOR(c.committed_at / 1000000000 / 86400) * 86400) AS time, CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY time, CASE WHEN c.method <> 'undetermined' THEN c.method ELSE COALESCE(c.reason, CASE WHEN c.status IN ('uninstrumented','unmatched','unassisted','degraded') THEN c.status END, 'undetermined') END ORDER BY time

metrics.title: Most agent-edited files
metrics.description: Per-file agent activity, from observed edits rather than commits. A file with many edits and few committed lines is one the agent iterated on heavily — that is effort, not output.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(file, '/', -1) AS file, COUNT(*) AS agent_edits, SUM(lines_added) AS lines_written FROM whodunit_events WHERE file <> '' AND observed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY file ORDER BY agent_edits DESC LIMIT 20

metrics.title: Agent activity by tool
metrics.description: Which operations agents performed. Read alongside the commit panels: a large edit count with low committed output means iteration, not productivity.

params_schema.name: time_from
params_schema.description: Start of the reporting window (epoch macro).

params_schema.name: time_to
params_schema.description: End of the reporting window (epoch macro).

metrics.sql: SELECT agent, tool, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(lines_added) AS lines_added, SUM(lines_removed) AS lines_removed FROM whodunit_events WHERE observed_at BETWEEN ? * 1000000000 AND ? * 1000000000 GROUP BY agent, tool ORDER BY events DESC

agent.query: SELECT DISTINCT agent FROM whodunit_sessions WHERE agent <> '' UNION SELECT DISTINCT agent FROM whodunit_events WHERE agent <> ''

board.query: SELECT name AS __text, id AS __value FROM boards ORDER BY name

contributor.query: SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '(unattributed)') AS __text, COALESCE(NULLIF(contributor, ''), '') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos ORDER BY 1

repo.query: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(r.name), LEFT(w.repo_id, 8)) AS __text, w.repo_id AS __value FROM whodunit_commits w LEFT JOIN repo_commits rc ON rc.commit_sha = w.commit_sha LEFT JOIN repos r ON r.id = rc.repo_id GROUP BY w.repo_id ORDER BY __text

team.query: SELECT __text, __value FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(wt.team_name, NULLIF(t.name, ''), '(unassigned)') AS __text, COALESCE(wt.team_name, NULLIF(t.name, ''), '(unassigned)') AS __value FROM whodunit_repos r LEFT JOIN team_users tu ON tu.user_id = r.contributor LEFT JOIN teams t ON t.id = tu.team_id LEFT JOIN whodunit_teams wt ON wt.contributor = r.contributor UNION SELECT '(unassigned)', '(unassigned)' ) options ORDER BY 1
